analysis: Examined base_text units for docs/architecture/inference.md lines 1629-2248 (MiMo, Flash-Next, Flint, Bonsai, code map). These lines are unchanged context; the only change is head lines 1030-1047, which document the new PromptTokenCache (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/PromptTokenCache.swift) in LocalTokenizerBridge: a per-prefix-cache-scope reuse cache of token IDs for rendered template pieces, parallel encoding on up to four cores, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma 4/GPT-OSS, load-time and sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on mismatch, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch. Security relevance: T-041/SEC-035 (cross-tenant cache sharing and TTFT oracle on A-001). The doc claims reuse never crosses a cache scope, which, if the scope equals the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, preserves cross-account isolation; same-scope reuse adds a tokenization-latency hit/miss signal of the same kind as the accepted same-account SEC-035 oracle. Unverified in this batch: (1) that the PromptTokenCache key actually includes the coordinator cacheSalt and not a caller-controlled prompt_cache_key/user field; (2) behavior when caching is disabled or no scope is present (standalone/local mode); (3) memory bounds/eviction of the in-RAM token-piece cache (availability, plaintext-derived tokens retained in process memory beyond request lifetime, relevant to T-028/T-014); (4) whether the threat model T-041 should document this new in-process plaintext-derived cache and its retention. Rewritten templates (ChatTemplateLoopRewrites) could diverge from served template output; doc states sampled comparisons disable reuse, but correctness of prompt-contract identity (sidecar parity) needs source review. No concrete regression is provable from documentation alone; source files are outside this batch.
